text: A chessboard has sixty-four squares arranged in eight rows and eight columns. A bishop moves diagonally across squares of the same color.
A potter shapes soft clay into a bowl and lets it dry. Firing the bowl in a kiln makes the clay hard and durable.
At a post office, letters are sorted by their destination addresses. A postage stamp shows that the sender has paid for delivery.
A woven fabric is made by interlacing two sets of threads. Threads running lengthwise are called the warp, while the crossing threads form the weft.
Molten rock beneath the surface of Earth is called magma. When it erupts from a volcano and reaches the surface, it is called lava.
A glacier forms where accumulated snow is compressed into ice over many years. Under its own weight, the ice slowly moves downhill.
A key must have the right shape to operate its matching lock. Turning the key allows the locking mechanism to release the door.
A trapeze artist swings from a suspended bar above the circus ring. A safety net below the performers helps protect them if they fall.
A balloon filled with helium can rise because helium is less dense than the surrounding air. A string keeps the balloon from drifting away.
A mint manufactures coins by pressing a design into pieces of metal. The two sides of a coin can carry different images and inscriptions.
During a trial, witnesses describe what they observed and lawyers present evidence. The jury considers that evidence before reaching a verdict.
In a printing press, ink is transferred onto sheets of paper. Movable type allows individual letters to be rearranged to print a different page.
Fencers wear protective masks and use specially designed sporting weapons. A referee oversees the bout and determines when a valid touch has been scored.
In a mechanical clock, gears transfer motion between connected parts. A pendulum can regulate that motion so the hands advance at a steady rate.
A perfume combines fragrant ingredients to create a particular scent. Keeping the bottle closed helps prevent its contents from evaporating.
Origami is the art of folding paper into recognizable shapes. A sequence of careful folds can turn a flat square into a paper crane.
